$comment: Canonical guidance invariants (evolution Step 09). Developer-only, never shipped. tools/validate/check-guidance.mjs implements the machine checks named here; docs/chayen/GUIDANCE_INVARIANTS.md explains diagnostics. Each invariant names its single authoritative source; other files may summarize it but must not contradict it.

invariants.name: task-contract-decision
invariants.statement: An unclear request (acceptance criteria not yet observable, or a needed fact unknown) is clarified in one message before any edit, however small. Then: any risky action gets a full contract; several files or layers get a proportional contract; a fully specified low-risk change gets no contract and no questions. Only the task-contract recipe states the eligibility rule in full.
machine: The recipe Procedure states clarification before any edit, however small, before its decision table.
The recipe decision table names the full, proportional and no-contract paths.
The entry skill's task-contract step names clarification before any edit and the three contract paths, and refers to the recipe.
The entry skill's References load condition for the recipe covers unclear requests.
No other file restates a file-count eligibility rule.
review: Whether a summary elsewhere is faithful in meaning, beyond the named anchors.

invariants.name: action-specific-approval
invariants.statement: Each risky action needs approval of that exact action and target before it is performed. Confirming a task description or a contract is never approval of a risky action.
machine: The recipe requires approval of the exact action and target, and says confirmation is never approval.
The implementation entry skill says contract approval is not approval of each risky action.
No shipped file says contract approval or confirmation covers, implies or counts as approval.
review: Approval wording phrased in a way the weakening patterns do not recognise.

invariants.name: acceptance-verdicts
invariants.statement: accept: fresh, adequate observed evidence shows the criterion is met. verify_more: evidence is missing, partial, stale, not reproducible or inadequate. revise: evidence contradicts the criterion.
machine: The recipe defines all three verdicts.

Every definitional clause ('accept when ...', 'accept: ...') in shipped content defines accept without missing, partial, stale or unexecuted evidence, verify_more with missing or partial evidence, and revise with contradicting evidence.
No shipped sentence marks missing, partial, stale, uncovered or unverified evidence as accept.
review: Verdict wording that does not use a definitional form.

invariants.name: completion-outcome
invariants.statement: DONE requires completed scope, required verification and every required acceptance criterion at accept. Otherwise PARTIAL or BLOCKED with the next safe action. Written code is never DONE by itself.
machine: The recipe defines DONE, PARTIAL and BLOCKED.
Every paragraph, list item or table row that defines when DONE applies also requires accept.
No shipped sentence makes DONE follow from written code, compilation or a green build alone.
review: Outcome vocabulary other than DONE, PARTIAL and BLOCKED.

invariants.name: check-status-honesty
invariants.statement: A check that was skipped, not run, blocked or of unknown outcome is never reported as PASS. Check statuses are distinct from acceptance verdicts.
machine: The testing skill's status table defines PASSED, FAILED, SKIPPED, BLOCKED, NOT_RUN and UNKNOWN, and its SKIPPED row says a skip is not a pass.
The change-summary recipe lists the same statuses and says an unexecuted check is never reported as passing.
No shipped sentence counts, treats, reports or marks a skipped, not-run, blocked or unknown check as a pass.
review: Status reporting in prose that avoids the recognised verbs.

invariants.name: source-of-truth-precedence
invariants.statement: System and developer instructions and provider permissions take priority; the user's authorized scope, repository instructions and conventions follow, before generic practice. Generated project knowledge (.chayen/) is a map: the current source wins when they disagree.
machine: Every SKILL.md has a Precedence principle that gives system and developer instructions and provider permissions priority.
Every shipped file outside chayen-init that tells the agent to read .chayen/profile.md or a .chayen/units/ file also says, in the same paragraph or list, that the source wins on disagreement.
No shipped sentence lets .chayen/ files override the source.
review: The relative order of repository instructions and conventions inside each Precedence principle.

invariants.name: advisory-not-enforcement
invariants.statement: Guidance is advisory. It never claims to enforce, guarantee, block or prevent anything; real controls (permissions, CI, scanners, reviews) do. Security-sensitive skills state this explicitly.
machine: No shipped sentence says this skill, guidance, recipe, checklist, workflow, template or these instructions enforce, guarantee, ensure, block, prevent or stop something (negated statements are allowed).
No shipped sentence claims fully, completely, 100% or guaranteed secure, safe or compliant.
The skills that carry an advisory statement today (security, data, devops, architecture, ai-engineering) keep one.
review: Enforcement claims with another grammatical subject, for example 'the agent will block ...'.

invariants.name: skill-ownership-and-handoff
invariants.statement: Hand-offs name an existing shipped skill in plain prose, never a link or provider invocation syntax; a skill never hands off to itself; a 'When not to use' row names a skill or a recognised non-skill outcome.
machine: Every chayen-* skill name in shipped content (outside the .chayen path) is a shipped skill.
No shipped content uses provider-specific invocation syntax (/plugin:skill, $skill, 'Skill tool').

Every 'When not to use' Better fit cell names existing skills other than its own, or a recognised outcome (answer directly, not covered, decline, no guidance, an em dash). Unrecognised cells are REVIEW.
review: Whether the named skill really owns the excluded request.

invariants.name: workflow-exit-and-verification
invariants.statement: Composite workflow exit checks never accept less evidence than the workflow's Verification rules: a stage that declares completion requires accepted criteria or explicit evidence, and the Verification section keeps the status vocabulary and the verdict rule.
machine: Every workflow Verification section keeps 'PASS, FAIL, NOT_RUN or N/A' and the one-verdict-per-criterion rule.
Exit checks are subject to GI-04 and GI-05.
An exit check that declares completion (done, complete, verified, closed) without an evidence term is REVIEW.
review: Whether each exit check is sufficient for its stage.

invariants.name: independent-evidence-audit
invariants.statement: The evidence audit is an independent review: the implementer's conclusions are claims, never evidence, and are re-checked by a reviewer who did not make the change. A test file is not a test run; a claimed PASS needs a recorded run; evidence older than the last relevant change is stale; interactive UI requirements need a behavioural check and access-control requirements their negative paths; a cited but unrecorded run is no evidence. Each criterion review records criterion, claim, evidence source, independent method, observed outcome, confidence limitation, verdict and next action. Quoted output is redacted, and an audit is no security guarantee.
machine: The Evidence audit section keeps the anchors for each rule in the statement.
The criterion review table keeps all eight fields.
No shipped file infers a test run or a pass from a test file (negation is checked in the predicate only).
No shipped file lets the implementer audit, approve or accept its own evidence.
review: Whether a summary of the audit elsewhere is faithful, beyond the named anchors.
Whether the required evidence is proportional to the criterion's risk.
